title: First Visit to an Absorbing Return State
statement: Let a Turing machine run from a configuration $start$ to a configuration $finish$ in $B$ steps. Suppose $finish$ has state $ret$, $start$ does not have state $ret$, and every configuration with state $ret$ is unchanged by one step. Then there is a positive time $t\le B$ such that the run reaches exactly $finish$ at time $t$, and no configuration at any earlier time has state $ret$.
hypotheses_covered: A Turing machine and start and finish configurations
A natural-number step bound $B$ and the run reaches $finish$ at exactly $B$ steps
The start configuration does not have state $ret$
Every configuration with state $ret$ is fixed by one step
replaced: Let a machine run from a start configuration to a finish configuration in $B$ steps, where the finish control is a distinguished absorbing return state, every configuration in that state is fixed by one step, and the start is not in the return state. Then there is a strictly positive time $t \le B$ at which the run first reaches the return state, and the configuration at $t$ is already the exact finish configuration.
